title: The Rooms We Learn to Want
sentences: Every flat I have lived in has taught me something new about domestic space.
The first was small enough that I could reach the kitchen without leaving my bed.
I assumed at the time that what I needed was simply somewhere rather larger.
The larger place, when I eventually got it, turned out to be oddly uncomfortable.
Rooms that nobody ever used made the whole flat feel permanently unfinished.
What I had actually wanted was a door I could close, not additional floor area.
Estate agents describe property almost entirely through numbers and dimensions.
Those numbers say nothing at all about where the light falls in the afternoon.
They cannot express the way a narrow corridor makes an entire household behave.
We buy square metres and then spend years discovering what we needed instead.
